channel.title: Farsçadan (English)
channel.description: AI-assisted English translations of selected stories from Iran's Persian-language press. Every story notes the outlet's political orientation.

item.title: Houthis announced strike on Riyadh and Jeddah; Saudi coalition calls claim 'misleading'
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Houthis announced missile and drone strikes on Riyadh and Jeddah; flights were suspended, Saudi coalition denied the claim. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: Fadavi: US Navy withdrew from Hormuz; that same evening, 'unauthorized' tanker was fired upon
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: General Fadavi announced the complete withdrawal of the US Navy from the region; that evening a tanker was reportedly fired upon in Hormuz. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: US withdraws all B-1 bombers from UK base amid terror plot investigation
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The US withdrew all B-1 bomber aircraft from the Fairford base in the UK, where a terror plot investigation is underway. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: Oil Minister Paknejad resigns; Pezeshkian appoints Hamid Bord as acting minister
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad resigned "for personal reasons"; President Pezeshkian appointed Hamid Bord as acting oil minister. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: Kalaibaf says he was 'shocked' by $10,000 currency distribution to all adults; subsidies committee formed
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Parliament Speaker Kalaibaf said he was shocked by the Central Bank's $10,000 currency subsidy decision; government forms pricing committee. (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: Pezeshkian: Government has reorganized to counter "the enemy's economic war"
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: President Pezeshkian said the government has reorganized the economy for "war conditions," shifting priority to livelihoods and stability. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Houthis strike Aramco, Saudi Arabia bombs Sanaa; fighting escalates in Taiz
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The Houthis hit Saudi Aramco facilities in Riyadh with missiles, Saudi jets bombed Sanaa, and fighting continues in Taiz. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: Closing the Strait of Hormuz: What does it gain Iran? Conflicting calculations in Tehran press
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Tehran newspapers debate whether closing the Strait of Hormuz benefits or harms Iran long-term; oil reached $103. (Source: Khabaronline)

item.title: US expels two Iranian UN diplomats for defying order to leave
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: According to Axios, the US expelled two Iranian UN diplomats who ignored an order to leave New York as tensions escalate. (Source: Donya-ye Eghtesad)

item.title: Dollar tops 270,000 tomans as prosecutors threaten currency dealers with arrest
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: In Tehran the dollar passed 269,000 and the euro 302,000 tomans for the first time; prosecutors threatened dealers, and the central bank said "temporary." (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Clashes in Zahedan and Rask: Sources contradict each other on the death toll
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The death toll from Oct. 1-2 clashes in Sistan-Baluchestan varies by source; the IRGC and opposition outlets reported different figures. (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: LNG shipments through Hormuz hit highest level since the war began
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: LNG shipments through Hormuz in September reached their highest monthly level since the war began in February, Reuters reports. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: US sends third aircraft carrier to Middle East in biggest buildup in 23 years
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has left for the Middle East; US forces in the region could top 60,000, the largest buildup since 2003. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: Trump's security team secretly discussed Iran and Yemen at Camp David
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Per Axios, Rubio, Hegseth, Witkoff, Ratcliffe and Caine discussed next steps in the Iran war at a meeting chaired by Vance. (Source: Khabaronline (via Axios))

item.title: Israel's "sword of Damocles" over Turkey: The Armenian genocide debate
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Israel's cabinet backed recognizing the Armenian genocide; Azerbaijan's mediation stalled it in the Knesset. Erdogan and Netanyahu clashed at the UN. (Source: Donya-ye Eghtesad)

item.title: US poll: 70% of adults say the Iran war "wasn't worth it"
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: An AP-NORC poll finds 69% of Americans don't think the Iran war is worth it; Democrats want the war budget cut. (Source: Ettelaat (via Al Jazeera and AP-NORC))

item.title: Appeals court upholds prison sentence for actress Elnaz Shakerdoost
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: An appeals court upheld Iranian actress Elnaz Shakerdoost's 1-year prison sentence over a post about the Dey protests. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Tanker hit off Oman: Persian press reports differ on the scale of the attack
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: UKMTO said a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile 4 miles east of Oman. Kayhan wrote that three UAE tankers had been targeted. (Source: ISNA)

item.title: On "snapback" anniversary, US and 55 countries issue joint statement; Tehran calls it "legally void"
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: On the anniversary of the return of UN sanctions, the US and its allies pledged to enforce arms and technology restrictions on Iran. (Source: Donya-ye Eghtesad)

item.title: Dollar nears 260,000 tomans; Central Bank of Iran says it will "intervene where necessary"
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The dollar rose more than 10% in a week in Tehran. The central bank began selling cash FX and the judiciary seized online price pages. (Source: Ettelaat)
